name: Lake Forest
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lake Forest, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Lake Forest, IL: the Market Square tree lighting, a Holiday Express train with Santa, Gorton Center shows and Elawa Farm crafts.
lede: Lake Forest opens the season the day after Thanksgiving, when a Home Alone screening at Gorton Center leads into the tree lighting in historic Market Square. December brings a Santa train from the Telegraph Road Metra station, a kids-only gift shop and holiday crafts and goats at Elawa Farm.
celebrates: Christmas in Lake Forest starts on the Friday after Thanksgiving. Gorton Center shows Home Alone in the afternoon, then families head to Market Square for the Tree Lighting Holiday Celebration, with kids' activities, visits with Santa, the Lake Forest Civic Orchestra, the Lake Forest High School Choristers and a Rockette-style number from Lake Forest Dance Academy just before the lights come on. In December, Lake Forest Parks and Recreation runs the Holiday Express, a Santa train ride from the West Lake Forest station to Fox Lake and back. Gorton Center adds its Kids Only Holiday Shop, ornament workshops and the Holly Jolly Concert, and Elawa Farm holds a Holiday Market with kids' crafts and goat cuddles.
lastyear: On Friday, November 28, 2025, the 41st Annual Tree Lighting came back to Market Square with a holiday movie at Gorton Community Center, Santa, carolers, kids' activities and dancers from Lake Forest Dance Academy, which marked its 50th anniversary that year. Gorton's Kids Only Holiday Shop followed on December 3, with high school Santa's Helpers guiding young shoppers and hot cocoa and cider for sale. Elawa Farm held its Holiday Market December 5 to 7 with a Holiday Craft-a-Palooza, and the park district's Holiday Express carried Santa to Fox Lake and back on December 20 and 21.
facts: The Lake Forest Tree Lighting began in Market Square in 1984. Architect Howard Van Doren Shaw designed the square, built in 1916 as one of the first shopping centers planned around cars. When the Lake Forest High School Choristers first sang at the lighting, 35 singers performed a cappella, and now more than 100 take part. The honor of flipping the switch has gone to mayors, residents, CROYA members and high school students. Gorton Center's theater is named for John and Nancy Hughes, a fun link to the John Hughes film Home Alone that opens the day.
trains: Lake Forest has two Metra stations. The Lake Forest station at 691 N. Western Avenue is on the Union Pacific North line, which runs from Chicago's Ogilvie Transportation Center to Kenosha. The station at 911 Telegraph Road, which the park district calls West Lake Forest, is on the Milwaukee District North line, and it is where the Holiday Express boards for its Santa ride to Fox Lake. Metra also runs decorated Holiday Trains on both lines. Farther afield, the Illinois Railway Museum in Union runs the Happy Holiday Railway, a ride with Santa and his elves through the winter countryside.

traditions: Gorton Center screens the John Hughes film Home Alone on the afternoon of the tree lighting.
Since 1984, families have gathered in Market Square to see the big tree lit, with Santa, carols and hot chocolate.
Lake Forest Dance Academy dancers perform a Rockette-style routine right before the tree lights up.
Children ages 4 to 10 shop for their families on their own at Gorton Center, and Wonder Wrappers wrap every gift.
Santa rides a park district train from West Lake Forest to Fox Lake and back, with games, sing-alongs and a reading of How the Grinch Stole Christmas.
Elawa Farm's December market adds kids' crafts, roasted chestnuts and visits with its goats.
kidfact: When the Lake Forest High School Choristers first sang at the tree lighting, there were 35 of them. Now more than 100 singers fill Market Square with carols.
faq: When is the Lake Forest tree lighting?

The Tree Lighting Holiday Celebration takes place in Market Square on the Friday after Thanksgiving, from 3 to 6 pm. Kids' activities start at 3, Santa visits from 3:15, and the tree is lit just after the Lake Forest Dance Academy performance at 5. A holiday movie at Gorton Community Center starts the day at 1 pm.
Is the Lake Forest tree lighting free?

Yes. The Friends of Lake Forest Parks and Recreation Foundation puts on the tree lighting as a free event, and local vendors sell food and hot drinks. It runs rain or shine, so dress for the weather. In past years the city has closed Western Avenue next to Market Square for the afternoon and made its parking lots free.
Can kids ride a train with Santa in Lake Forest?

Yes. Lake Forest Parks and Recreation runs the Holiday Express, a round trip from the West Lake Forest station on Telegraph Road to Fox Lake and back. Santa rides along, and there are holiday games, sing-alongs and a reading of How the Grinch Stole Christmas. Every rider, child or adult, needs a ticket, and children must ride with an adult.
What is the Kids Only Holiday Shop?

It is a Gorton Center tradition for children ages 4 to 10. Elves walk each child through a boutique of local vendors so they can buy gifts for family on their own, and Wonder Wrappers wrap and label each one. Most items cost $5 to $15, so send a gift list and small bills. Parents wait downstairs in the Card Room.
Which Metra stations serve Lake Forest?

Lake Forest has two. The station at 691 N. Western Avenue is on the Union Pacific North line, between Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago and Kenosha. The station at 911 Telegraph Road is on the Milwaukee District North line, the same line the Holiday Express rides to Fox Lake. Metra lists both stations as accessible.
What holiday events are at Elawa Farm?

Elawa Farm at 1401 Middlefork Drive holds a Holiday Market on December weekends with local makers, seasonal greenery, roasted chestnuts and Elawa-made pastries. Kids can drop in to the Holiday Craft-a-Palooza craft studio, and on some weekends families can book Hooves and Hugs sessions to pet and cuddle the farm's goats.
